name: Rivaroxaban
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Rivaroxaban dosing depends on creatinine clearance (CrCl), calculated with actual body weight. For atrial fibrillation the US label uses 15 mg once daily at CrCl 50 mL/min or less, including people on hemodialysis; for venous clots it advises avoiding use below CrCl 15 mL/min.
kidney_function_basis: Label uses creatinine clearance (CrCl, mL/min; Cockcroft–Gault with actual weight).

bands.recommendation: Atrial fibrillation (AF): 20 mg once daily with the evening meal. Deep vein thrombosis/pulmonary embolism (DVT/PE) treatment: 15 mg twice daily for 21 days, then 20 mg once daily (label).
AF: CrCl >50, 20 mg once daily; CrCl ≤50, 15 mg once daily with evening meal. DVT/PE and prophylaxis: no change while CrCl ≥15 (label).
AF: 15 mg once daily (not studied below CrCl 30, but expected exposure similar to CrCl 30–50) (label). DVT/PE treatment and prophylaxis: usual dosing while CrCl ≥15.

AF: label 15 mg once daily (based on pharmacokinetics). DVT/PE treatment, recurrence reduction and prophylaxis: avoid (label). Coronary/peripheral artery disease 2.5 mg twice daily: no CrCl adjustment.

hd: AF: 15 mg once daily gives concentrations similar to ROCKET AF (label; efficacy and safety unknown, dialysis patients not enrolled). Literature: 10 mg once daily in anuric hemodialysis patients gave exposure similar to 20 mg in healthy volunteers (De Vriese 2015). DVT/PE: avoid (CrCl <15). Specialist decision.
pd: No data in label. Insufficient data: specialist input.
crrt: No data in label. Insufficient data: specialist input.
dialyzable: No: high protein binding; hemodialysis had no significant effect on exposure (label; De Vriese 2015).

pediatric.approved_ages: VTE treatment and reduction in risk of recurrent VTE: birth to <18 years (after at least 5 days of parenteral anticoagulation). Thromboprophylaxis after Fontan procedure: 2 years and older (label).
pediatric.usual_dose: Body-weight-tiered fixed doses of tablet or oral suspension (label Table 2); no single mg/kg dose. Under 6 months: only if born at ≥37 weeks, ≥10 days of oral feeding, and ≥2.6 kg.
pediatric.max_dose: Adult dosing caps apply to the heaviest tier (see label Table 2).

renal.recommendation: 1 year and older: avoid if eGFR <50 mL/min/1.73 m2 (limited data) (label).

pediatric.neonates: Under 1 year: avoid if serum creatinine is above the 97.5th percentile for age (label Table 4, e.g., week 2 0.52 mg/dL; months 3–9 0.34 mg/dL).
pediatric.notes: eGFR 50–59 band: usual weight-tiered dosing; below 50 avoid.
pediatric.egfr_equation: Bedside Schwartz: eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m2) = 0.413 x height (cm) / serum creatinine (mg/dL)

adult: KEY CONFLICT: label 15 mg once daily for AF in hemodialysis vs De Vriese 2015 (n=18) showing 10 mg once daily reproduces 20 mg exposure in healthy volunteers. Choose the site's position.
Our 30–59 band straddles the label's CrCl 50 cutoff for AF; split explained in the text.
Selected label NDA215859 is the Xarelto oral suspension/tablet combined label (Sept 2026).
pediatric: Pediatric threshold is eGFR <50 (not <30) — stricter than apixaban. Equation not named in the rivaroxaban label; bedside Schwartz assumed.
Weight-tier table not transcribed; link to label.
